readings.title: The Mockery of the Exiled
readings.subtitle: Iyoḇ observes how those driven from societal order now treat his physical affliction with utter contempt.
readings.text: [Job 30:1] “But now they laugh at me, those younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs. [2] Of what use to me is the strength of their hands, since their manhood power has perished? [3] They are dried up from lack and hunger, they flee to a parched land, formerly a waste and ruin. [4] They pluck <dn>את</dn> salt herbs by the bushes, and broom tree roots for their food. [5] They were driven out from among men, they shouted at them as at a thief, [6] to dwell in the gullies of wadis, holes of the ground and clefts. [7] Among the bushes they cry out, under the nettles they huddled together – [8] sons of fools, even sons without a name, they have been whipped out of the land.

readings.title: The Breach of the Hedge
readings.subtitle: Stripped of divine protection, Iyoḇ becomes a song of derision as ruinous forces pursue his life.
readings.text: [Job 30:9] And now I have become their song, and I am a byword to them. [10] They have loathed me, they have kept far from me, and did not refrain from spitting in my face. [11] Because <dn>He</dn> has loosed <dn>את</dn> my bowstring and afflicted me, they have thrown off restraint in my presence. [12] At my right hand a brood rises; they pushed away my feet, and they raise up against me their destructive ways. [13] They have broken up my path, they gain by my ruin; no one restrains them. [14] They come as through a wide breach; rushing on me under the ruins. [15] Destructions are turned upon me; they pursue my life as the wind, and my welfare has passed like a cloud.

readings.title: A Petition in the Whirlwind
readings.subtitle: Perceiving his suffering as severe divine opposition, Iyoḇ cries out as his physical state deteriorates toward the grave.
readings.text: [Job 30:16] And now my life pours itself out; days of affliction seize me. [17] My bones have been pierced in me at night, and my gnawings never lie down. [18] By great exertion is <dn>את</dn> my garment changed – it girds me as the collar of my coat, [19] throwing <dn>את</dn> me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes. [20] I cry out to <dn>You</dn>, but <dn>You</dn> do not answer me; I stand up, but <dn>You</dn> only look at me. [21] <dn>You</dn> have become cruel to me; with the power of <dn>Your</dn> hand <dn>You</dn> oppose me. [22] <dn>You</dn> lift me up to the wind, making me to ride it; and <dn>You</dn> melt me in a storm. [23] For I have known that <dn>You</dn> bring me to death, and to the house of appointment for all living.

readings.title: The Reversal of Restorative Harmony
readings.subtitle: Despite his past commitment to premial compassion, his days are now consumed by darkness, mourning, and severe biological distress.
readings.text: [Job 30:24] Yet does not one in a heap of ruins stretch out his hand, or in calamity cry out for help? [25] Did I not weep for him who was in trouble? Was my being not grieved for the poor? [26] When I looked for good, then evil came to me. And when I waited for light, darkness came. [27] My inward parts boiled and did not rest; days of affliction went before me. [28] I went about blackened, but not by the sun; I stood up in the assembly, I cried for help. [29] I became a brother of jackals, and a companion of ostriches. [30] My skin became black upon me, and my bones burned with heat. [31] So my lyre becomes mourning, and my flute the sound of weeping.

readings.title: The Covenant of the Eyes
readings.subtitle: Iyoḇ affirms his strict personal accountability, recognizing that Eloah meticulously numbers his every step.
readings.text: [Job 31:1] “I have made <dn>את</dn> a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze at a maiden? [2] For what is the portion of <dn>Eloah</dn> from above, and the inheritance of <dn>the Almighty</dn> from on high? [3] Is it not calamity to the perverse, and strangeness to the workers of wickedness? [4] Does <dn>He</dn> not see <dn>את</dn> my ways, and number <dn>את</dn> all my steps?

readings.title: The Righteous Scales of Justice
readings.subtitle: Calling upon the exact extraction of justice, Iyoḇ invites divine weighing to prove his innocence regarding deceit and illicit desire.
readings.text: [Job 31:5] If I have walked with <dn>את</dn> falsehood, or if my foot has hurried to deceit, [6] let <dn>Him</dn> weigh me in a right scale, and let <dn>Eloah</dn> know my integrity. [7] If my step does turn from the way, or my heart has gone after my eyes, or if <dn>את</dn> any spot has clung to my hands, [8] let me sow, and another eat; and let my harvest be rooted out. [9] If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if I have lurked at my neighbour’s door, [10] let my wife grind for another, and let others bow down over her. [11] For that would be a wicked scheme, and a punishable crookedness. [12] For that would be a fire that burns to destruction, and take root among all my increase.

readings.title: The Equality of the Created Form
readings.subtitle: He acknowledges that true justice demands the equitable treatment of all servants, fashioned by the same Creator in the womb.
readings.text: [Job 31:13] If I have refused <dn>את</dn> the plea of my male servant or my female servant when they complained against me, [14] then what should I do when <dn>Ěl</dn> rises up? And when <dn>He</dn> punishes, what should I answer <dn>Him</dn>? [15] Did not <dn>He</dn> who made me in the womb make him? And did not One fashion us in the womb?

readings.title: The Guarantee to the Vulnerable
readings.subtitle: Rehearsing his continual provision for the fatherless and the widow, Iyoḇ details his adherence to restorative economic principles.
readings.text: [Job 31:16] If I have withheld <dn>את</dn> the poor from pleasure, or caused the widow’s eyes to fail, [17] or eaten <dn>את</dn> my piece of bread by myself, and the fatherless did not eat of it – [18] but from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided her – [19] if I have seen <dn>את</dn> anyone perish for lack of garments, or a poor one without covering; [20] if his loins have not blessed me, and he warmed himself with the fleece of my sheep; [21] if I have raised <dn>את</dn> my hand against the fatherless, when I saw I had help in the gate; [22] let my arm fall from my shoulder, and my arm be broken from the bone. [23] For I am in dread of destruction from <dn>Ěl</dn>, and from <dn>His</dn> excellence I could not escape.

readings.title: The Folly of Wealth and Celestial Idolatry
readings.subtitle: He utterly denies placing his trust in the false security of gold or participating in the pagan worship of the sun and moon.
readings.text: [Job 31:24] If I have put <dn>את</dn> my trust in gold, or called fine gold my refuge; [25] if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gained much; [26] if I have looked at <dn>את</dn> the sun when it shines, or the moon moving in brightness, [27] so that my heart has been secretly enticed, and my mouth has kissed my hand – [28] that too is a punishable crookedness, for I would have denied <dn>Ěl</dn> above.

readings.title: The Refusal of Retribution and Concealment
readings.subtitle: Operating contrary to a retributive penal system, he affirms he has never rejoiced over an enemy’s ruin nor hidden his transgressions like Aḏam.
readings.text: [Job 31:29] If I have rejoiced when he who hated me was ruined, or lifted myself up when evil found him – [30] also I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for a curse on his life – [31] if the men of my tent did not say, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’ [32] The stranger did not have to spend the night in the street, for I have opened my doors to the way. [33] If I have covered <dn>את</dn> my transgressions like Aḏam, by hiding my crookedness in my bosom, [34] then let me fear the great crowd, and dread the scorn of clans, then I would be silent, and go out of the door!

readings.title: The Signed Guarantee of Innocence
readings.subtitle: Approaching his Creator like a prince, Iyoḇ seals his testimony and demands a formal written indictment from his accuser.
readings.text: [Job 31:35] Who would give me a hearing? See, my signature, let <dn>the Almighty</dn> answer me, and let my accuser write a bill! [36] Would I not take <dn>את</dn> it up on my shoulder, bind it on me for a crown? [37] I would declare to <dn>Him</dn> <dn>את</dn> the number of my steps – I would approach <dn>Him</dn> like a prince. [38] If my land cries out against me, or its furrows weep together; [39] if I have eaten <dn>את</dn> its fruit without payment, or caused its owners to die; [40] let thistles grow instead of wheat, and useless weed instead of barley.” The <dn>את</dn> words of Iyoḇ are ended.
